findings.title: Automated suite does not prove fresh-prompt consistency
findings.criterion_ref: PKGV2-T10 requires the automated suite to “positively prove PKGV2-T01 through PKGV2-T09”; PKGV2-T03 expressly includes the N30 prompt’s read-only ownership language.
findings.trigger: A fresh prompt becomes inconsistent with the graph’s ownership or graph binding. No test reads or validates any of the three fresh prompts, so the suite remains green.
findings.consequence: The automated gate can approve an execution prompt that authorizes the wrong owner or directs execution against a stale/nonexistent graph. The current bundle demonstrates the blind spot: N00, N20, and N30 reference `execution_package_v2/implementation.graph.v1.yaml`, although the package contains and binds `implementation.graph.v4.yaml`; N20/N30’s instructed scans therefore fail instead of verifying their nodes.
findings.evidence: The test section, lines 1395–2266, defines graph/scanner/validator paths but no prompt paths or prompt-content assertions. Meanwhile lines 2318–2321 require nonexistent `execution_package_v2/implementation.graph.v1.yaml`; lines 2397–2399 and 2450 instruct N20 to scan with it; lines 2571–2574 do the same for N30. The graph and scanner identify `implementation.graph.v4.yaml` at lines 49, 256–337, and 471.

observations: The bundle’s fenced copies contain one additional separator newline relative to the source-file byte counts/hashes in `manifest.v1.json`; the substantive embedded text otherwise matches the live originals. No numbered criterion is defeated by that newline.

The live validator reports `valid: true`. Under the read-only environment, 85 non-temporary tests passed; the two excluded tests are the inspected synthetic-tree tests requiring pytest’s temporary-directory fixture, which cannot run without a writable temporary directory.

I did not classify the stale prompt graph filenames as a standalone PKGV2-T01 or PKGV2-T03 failure: T01 explicitly scopes graph binding to the scanner, graph verification lists, and validator, while T03’s required N30 ownership language is substantively correct. Their reportable impact is the T10 automated-proof gap.
reasoning: PKGV2-T00 through T09 otherwise survived inspection: historical hashes and git scope were intact; scanner default/path arithmetic and narrowing logic were correct; graph ownership, scan modes, result roots, source-spec digest, and write-set uniqueness were correct; and validator argument counting handles separated, equals, and abbreviated forms. The suite is real and largely passing, but it never examines the fresh prompts and therefore cannot positively prove the prompt component of T03. The existing stale graph instructions make that omission operationally material, so the T10 defect meets the major threshold.
